The Story of Sukoshal Muni

I bow to Lord Jinendra, the purifier of the world, to the word of Jina, and to the gurus, and I write the story of Sukoshal Muni.

In Ayodhya, during the reign of King Prajapal, there lived a famous merchant named Siddharth. He had thirty-two beautiful wives, but by ill fortune, none of them had any children. However beautiful and virtuous a wife may be, without children she lacks splendour — just as a creeper without fruit and flowers lacks beauty.

Among these wives, the one whom the merchant loved most — Jayaavati — was always worshipping false gods for a son. One day, a monk saw her worshipping false gods and said to her, "Sister, the hope you have from worshipping these false gods will not be fulfilled. The cause of all good things — wealth, prosperity, children, health, honour, good intellect — is merit. So if you seek a means to gain merit, that would be better. I tell you this for your welfare: abandon the worship of these yakshas and false gods, which does not bind merit, and take faith in Jain dharma. Thus you will come to the truth, and your wish will begin to be fulfilled." The monk also told her, "The thing you desire will certainly be yours within seven years. Abandon worry and practise dharma."

Jayaavati was pleased by the monk's teaching. From that day, she developed faith in Jain dharma. The monk's final words filled her with great joy — for what she had longed for in her heart was now about to be fulfilled!

The monk's words proved true. Through the grace of dharma, Jayaavati gave birth to a son. He was named Sukoshal. Sukoshal was handsome and radiant.

Merchant Siddharth, having indulged in sensual pleasures, had grown old. The knowledge-filled eyes of his heart had shown him the true nature of the world and frightened him greatly. He did not wish to remain in the world even for a moment, but having no one to manage his wealth, he had to stay home until his son came of age. Now that Sukoshal had grown, he was overjoyed. He soon arranged his son's marriage and, once Sukoshal was settled, Siddharth took initiation as a monk. Through intense austerity and meditation, he destroyed his karmas and attained liberation.

Sukoshal, seeing his father's example, also became detached from worldly life. He gave his wealth to the worthy, took initiation, and became a monk. Through dedicated spiritual practice, Sukoshal Muni destroyed his karmas and attained liberation.

This story teaches that the worship of false gods cannot bring true benefit. Only through merit — gained by practising true dharma — can one's wishes be fulfilled. Jayaavati's switch from false worship to Jain dharma brought her the son she desired. And both husband and son, recognising the impermanence of worldly life, ultimately found the path to liberation.
